author: Mark Atwood
text:
Root-caused conclusively. It is a hickory bug, and specifically a MUST NOT violation.

debian.org is mid algorithm rollover: the parent DS set holds only 40756 8 2 (algorithm 8), while the zone publishes DNSKEYs at BOTH algorithm 8 and algorithm 13 (two KSKs, two ZSKs), and the DNSKEY RRset is signed by keytags 40756 and 29764. So there is an algorithm signalled in the DNSKEY RRset with nothing in the parent to chain it to.

Isolated the variable rather than assuming it. The three zones that validate are single-algorithm: huque.com is DS 13 / DNSKEY 13 only, freebsd.org is DS 8 / DNSKEY 8 only. debian.org is the only one with an uncovered algorithm. Same resolver, anchors, upstream and process -- so it is not the environment, the anchors, or the zone being broken.

RFC 6840 4.11 settles both halves. The configuration is legal: 'It is possible to add algorithms at the DNSKEY that aren't in the DS record, but not vice versa.' And the validator behaviour is mandated: 'Validators SHOULD accept any single valid path. They SHOULD NOT insist that all algorithms signaled in the DS RRset work, and they MUST NOT insist that all algorithms signaled in the DNSKEY RRset work.' hickory insists, so it throws away the valid algorithm-8 path because algorithm 13 has nothing to chain to. That is the MUST NOT.

Not worked around, and the reason is already project policy rather than a new judgement. The obvious workaround is to believe the upstream AD bit, which 9.9.9.9 does set on these answers -- but this crate's own documented stance is that an AD bit is a claim by a host on the network path and accepting it 'would reduce DANE to the security of the link to that host'. That applies to every answer, not just this one, so trading it away to recover one zone is the wrong trade. Validation happens inside hickory, so there is no third option from here.

Documented in pkix-dane-resolver's crate docs with the reproduction, the spec citation, what it costs (Indeterminate folds into insecure, so DANE silently stops applying under RFC 7672), and the diagnostic an operator should run before concluding the problem is local.

Leaving this OPEN: it is an unfixed upstream defect, not a resolved one. The remaining action is reporting it to hickory, which is outward-facing and needs Mark's go-ahead. pkix-dane-resolver 0.3.0 carries the documentation.
